title: E6 R2 · plan sizing on Grok
subtitle: Does the generic step bound (Cg) split oversized plans without over-splitting small ones? Grok 4.7 medium, 4 samples per arm.

notes.text: R2 launched: K2, K4, K6, K7 × arms T and Cg × 4 samples, 4 lanes
Lanes K4 and K6-K7 relaunched: run refuses --sample with --samples
Live card started: Claude pushes a new state on every 3.5-minute check
K2 control ended 0, 1, 0, 1 (bar 0.5): Cg wins K2 if its sample 4 lands in band
Freed lane took K7 samples 3-4 so the K6-K7 lane is no longer the bottleneck
K2 decided: Cg supports, 0.75 vs 0.50 with noise 0; the margin is one sample
Second freed lane took K7 sample 2; R2 now ends about 11:15
R2 complete: K2 supports Cg; K4, K6 and K7 at the ceiling in both arms; all 32 slices passed
Cg's gate refused nothing in 28 samples: the countable prose did the work. Grok handed to E-EFF1

findings.title: The control reproduces the defect
findings.text: T kept the K1 engine in 2 steps in 3 of 4 samples, one with 9 criteria

findings.title: A countable bound moves Grok
findings.text: B, C and Cg put 10 of 12 K1 plans in band, against 1 of 4 for T

findings.title: The gate never fired
findings.text: 0 refusals in 24 samples: the prose bound did all the work

findings.title: No over-splitting
findings.text: Every bug fix stays 1 step; board layers always stay apart

findings.title: Generic wording wins K2
findings.text: Cg 0.75 vs T 0.50 on the Node engine, noise 0; the margin is one sample

findings.title: Verdicts measure the planner, not Improve
findings.text: Improve changed no step count in 79 samples; the largest step grew 0 characters at the median

findings.title: Improve skips the size limits
findings.text: An Improve-revised result bypasses the producer bounds: K4 Cg 2 S1 grew 846 → 1,221 of 1,200 (main too)

findings.title: Fat criteria dodge the count
findings.text: Cg on K2 kept 2 criteria per step but wrote 1,121 characters in them

findings.title: The bound can swing to many tiny steps
findings.text: Cg K2 sample 2: 10 one-behaviour steps; in band, but each step costs an implement and an Improve round
